name: Ohio
note: The funeral director registers the death with the local registrar through the Department of Health's electronic death registration system within five working days, after the attending physician (or the coroner for reportable deaths) certifies the cause within 48 hours. A burial permit cannot issue without the certificate. The Department of Health then reports adult deaths monthly to the Secretary of State, whose reports trigger cancellation by county boards of elections, and makes death SSNs available to Medicaid. Death certificates are public records.

citations.title: Determination of death by certified nurse practitioner or clinical nurse specialist
citations.quote: A certified nurse-midwife, certified nurse practitioner, or clinical nurse specialist may determine and pronounce an individual's death.

citations.title: Determination of death by physician assistant
citations.quote: The physician assistant shall notify the individual's attending physician of the determination and pronouncement of death

citations.title: Notice to coroner of violent, suspicious, unusual or sudden death
citations.quote: shall immediately notify the office of the coroner of the known facts concerning the time, place, manner, and circumstances of the death

citations.title: Prohibited acts
citations.quote: No physician other than the coroner in the county in which a death, or a fetal death of at least twenty weeks of gestation, occurs

citations.title: Statement of facts in certificates - death certificate
citations.quote: Each death or fetal death that occurs in this state shall be registered with the local registrar of vital statistics

citations.title: Medical certificate of death within forty-eight hours
citations.quote: within forty-eight hours after notification of the death or fetal death

citations.title: Social security number on the death certificate
citations.quote: Any death certificate registered pursuant to this section shall contain the social security number of the decedent, if available.

citations.title: Medical certification of cause of death
citations.quote: completed and certified by the attending physician who attended the deceased, or by the coroner, within forty-eight hours after death

citations.title: Filing of the certificate of death when the cause of death is not known
citations.quote: enter " pending" or "pending - not drug related" in the cause of death portion, and return the certificate to the funeral director

citations.title: Investigation of delayed filing of certificates of death and fetal death
citations.quote: A satisfactory and complete death certificate shall be filed within five working days after the date of death.

citations.title: Director shall prescribe forms
citations.quote: The director shall prescribe electronic methods and forms for obtaining registration of births, deaths, and other vital statistics

citations.title: Burial permit required - records to be kept
citations.quote: No such permit shall be issued by a local registrar or sub-registrar until a satisfactory death, fetal death, or provisional death certificate is filed

citations.title: Penalty
citations.quote: Whoever violates division (C), (E), (F), or (G) of section 3705.29 of the Revised Code shall be fined not more than one thousand dollars

citations.title: Keeping and transmitting records by local registrar
citations.quote: each fetal death and death certificate printed on paper that the local registrar receives from the electronic death registration system (EDRS)

citations.title: Transmission to the state office of vital statistics
citations.quote: The local registrar shall transmit to the state office of vital statistics all original fetal death and death certificates received

citations.title: Notice of communicable-disease deaths
citations.quote: notify the health commissioner with jurisdiction in the registration district of the receipt of a death certificate attesting that death resulted from a communicable disease

citations.title: Social security numbers made available to child support and Medicaid
citations.quote: For the purpose of eligibility determinations for medical assistance programs as defined in section 5160.01 of the Revised Code, the department of medicaid.

citations.title: Matching of birth and death records
citations.quote: post the facts of death to the appropriate birth record

citations.title: Copies of vital records
citations.quote: issue a certified copy of a vital record, or of a part of a vital record, in the director's or registrar's custody to any applicant

citations.title: Social security number withheld from copies for five years
citations.quote: For the first five years after a decedent's death, a decedent's social security number shall not be included on a certified copy

citations.title: Access to preliminary birth and death data
citations.quote: have access to preliminary birth and death data maintained by the department of health

citations.title: Cancellation of registration: director of health's monthly death report
citations.quote: the director of health shall file with the secretary of state the names, social security numbers, dates of birth, dates of death, and residences

citations.title: Cancellation of registration by the board of elections
citations.quote: the board of elections shall promptly cancel the registration of each elector named in the report

steps.title: Nurse or physician assistant pronounces death and notifies the attending practitioner
steps.who: A certified nurse-midwife, certified nurse practitioner or clinical nurse specialist; a registered nurse or physician assistant only in hospice/palliative care (and, for a PA, in nursing homes and similar facilities) where functions are not artificially sustained. Physicians pronounce under general medical practice.

deadline.text: not later than twenty-four hours following the pronouncement

steps.summary: Ohio lets advanced practice nurses pronounce death, and lets hospice RNs and physician assistants do so in defined settings. An RN or PA who pronounces may not complete any part of the death certificate and must notify the attending practitioner within 24 hours so the cause can be certified.

steps.title: Report a violent, suspicious, sudden or unusual death to the coroner
steps.who: The physician, nurse-midwife, CNS or CNP in attendance, any health care worker caring for the person, ambulance/emergency squad members and law enforcement; the funeral director if cremation is requested.
steps.trigger: Death by criminal or violent means, casualty, suicide, in a suspicious or unusual manner, suddenly in apparent good health, or of a person with a developmental disability.
steps.summary: These deaths must be reported to the county coroner at once. Only the coroner (or medical examiner) may then certify the cause, unless after a preliminary examination the coroner declines jurisdiction, and no other physician may certify a death from other than natural causes.

steps.title: Attending physician certifies the cause of death on the certificate
steps.who: The attending physician, or if none, the physician who last examined or treated the decedent (in person or by telehealth).
steps.trigger: The funeral director presents the death certificate for certification.

deadline.text: within forty-eight hours after notification of the death

steps.summary: The funeral director presents the certificate and the physician completes and signs the medical certificate within 48 hours, which may be done with an electronic signature.

steps.title: Coroner certifies the cause of death, or certifies it as pending
steps.who: The county coroner, deputy coroner, medical examiner or deputy medical examiner.
steps.trigger: A death within R.C. 313.12 is presented for certification.

deadline.text: within forty-eight hours after notification; supplementary certification within six months

steps.summary: The coroner certifies within 48 hours, entering "pending" when results are not known within five days of death, and later files a supplementary medical certification with the local registrar.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate with the local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director or other person in charge of final disposition, who obtains the personal particulars from the best qualified persons or sources available.
steps.trigger: The death; the certificate must be filed before a burial permit issues.

deadline.text: within five working days after the date of death

steps.summary: Registration is with the local registrar of the district where the death occurred, through the Department of Health's electronic death registration system (EDRS). The certificate carries the decedent's social security number if available. Refusal to comply with the chapter is punishable by a fine of up to $1,000 or up to a year's imprisonment, and the local registrar may report a late filer to its licensing agency.

steps.title: Local registrar issues the burial permit
steps.who: The local registrar or sub-registrar of vital statistics.
steps.trigger: Filing of a satisfactory death certificate, or a provisional certificate when the cause cannot be certified before burial.
steps.summary: No body may be interred, cremated or otherwise disposed of until the registrar issues a burial permit, which requires a filed certificate. A provisional certificate can secure a burial permit, but not one for cremation, and the complete certificate must follow within five days of death.

steps.title: Local registrar transmits death certificates to the state Office of Vital Statistics
steps.who: The local registrar of vital statistics.

deadline.text: on the state transmittal schedule set by the Department of Health

steps.summary: The local registrar numbers certificates with the EDRS number and transmits the originals to the state office, which examines them and keeps a permanent index of all deaths.

steps.title: Local registrar notifies the health commissioner of a communicable-disease death
steps.who: The local registrar, to the health commissioner with jurisdiction in the registration district.
steps.trigger: Receipt of a death certificate attesting death from a communicable disease.
steps.summary: A communicable-disease death is reported on to the local health commissioner as soon as the certificate is received.

steps.title: State registrar posts the fact of death to the birth record
steps.who: The director of health / state registrar.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death of a person born in Ohio.
steps.summary: The Department of Health may match birth and death records, post the death to the birth record and mark copies of the birth record "deceased", to prevent fraudulent use of a dead person's birth certificate.

steps.title: Director of Health reports adult deaths to the Secretary of State monthly
steps.who: The director of health, to the secretary of state, through a jointly established secure electronic system.
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons over eighteen in Ohio or another state since the last filing.

deadline.text: not later than the last day of each month

steps.summary: Each month the Department of Health files the names, social security numbers, dates of birth and death and residences of all adults who died, with a supplemental report for deaths notified late.

steps.title: Secretary of State reports deceased electors to county boards, which cancel registrations
steps.who: The secretary of state, to each county board of elections.
steps.trigger: The monthly death reports, together with data from SSA, SAVE and the STEVE interstate exchange.
steps.summary: The secretary of state sends each board a monthly report of registered electors who have died, and the board must promptly cancel each one's registration.

steps.title: Office of Vital Statistics makes death-certificate SSNs available to the Department of Medicaid
steps.who: The office of vital statistics, to the Ohio Department of Medicaid (and to the child support division of the Department of Job and Family Services).
steps.trigger: Registration of a death certificate carrying a social security number.
steps.summary: Social security numbers on registered death certificates must be made available to the Department of Medicaid for medical-assistance eligibility determinations and to child support enforcement.

steps.title: Department of Health gives boards of health access to preliminary death data
steps.who: The state registrar, to each city or general health district board of health and the Department of Children and Youth.
steps.trigger: Ongoing; preliminary data in the electronic vital records systems.
steps.summary: Local boards of health must have access to preliminary death data and the state's electronic vital records systems, in a format that permits geocoding, subject to a data use agreement.

steps.title: Certified copies issued to any applicant
steps.who: The director of health, the state registrar or a local registrar.
steps.trigger: A signed application and the fee.
steps.summary: Ohio death records are public: a certified copy goes to any applicant on application and fee. For five years after death the decedent's social security number is left off unless requested by the spouse, a lineal descendant, the executor or another listed person.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five working days after death (Ohio Adm. Code 3701-5-08); the statute itself requires filing before a burial permit issues and five days after death when a provisional certificate was used.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or other person in charge of final disposition registers; personal particulars come from the best qualified persons or sources.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate; the coroner certifies only R.C. 313.12 deaths.

electronicRegistration.note: The Department of Health's electronic death registration system (EDRS) issues the certificate number; certifiers may sign electronically. Paper-printed certificates are still filed locally until EDRS can issue an electronic copy.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state vital records index is the record.

governmentPropagation.note: State law drives a monthly feed to the Secretary of State for voter-roll cancellation and makes death SSNs available to Medicaid and child support. Feeds to SSA are in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Any applicant may obtain a certified copy; only the SSN is withheld for five years.

gaps: No Ohio statute found requiring the Bureau of Motor Vehicles to cancel a driver licence on a death report, or the Department of Taxation to be notified; not searched exhaustively.
The state-to-SSA electronic death registration (EDR) feed is not mentioned in R.C. ch. 3705; it is left to the us-federal layer.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately omitted so the us-federal value (LADMF) applies; Ohio law adds no private-sector route beyond open certified copies (R.C. 3705.23).
Physician pronouncement itself is not codified; only the nurse and PA pronouncement statutes were cited.
